recommendation: Keep the published source fix. It removes a stale meta.profile/tag implication from an active narrative example while preserving the already-correct ElementDefinition code semantics; no broader discriminator model change is needed for this issue.
issue_request: FHIR-13399 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution for FHIR-core ElementDefinition/StructureDefinition. It asked to make profile/targetProfile slicing explicit and to clarify that profile slicing is evaluated by validation against applicable profiles, not solely by checking Resource.meta.profile.
initial_application: svn revision 13385, represented by git commit d4d7fd1550c21ef9786b82d8f86b40fff78ae1b9, updated the DiscriminatorType.profile definition in source/datatypes/elementdefinition.xml to state that .resolve() uses the reference targetProfile and requires validation by possible profiles. The same application touched the profiling example but left the active example saying profile discriminator entries were differentiated by a profile tag.
additional_context: source/datatypes/elementdefinition.xml is active normative ElementDefinition source through source/fhir.ini, and source/profiling.html is an active built narrative page through source/hierarchy.xml. Later FHIR-23035 work clarified resolve()/targetProfile behavior on the same profiling page and did not reverse FHIR-13399. Zulip discussion quoted the old profile-tag wording while implementers asked how targetProfile slicing works and later discussed meta.profile as a workaround, supporting that the old example remained ambiguous.
reconciliation: Changed source/profiling.html's List.entry profile-discriminator example from profile-tag wording to conformance wording: entries are differentiated by whether the target resource conforms to the profile declared for the slice's item reference. No change was made to the DiscriminatorType.profile code definition because it already contains the requested targetProfile and validation language.
source_changes: source/profiling.html: clarified the List.entry profile discriminator example to use target resource conformance to the slice's declared reference profile instead of profile-tag wording.

related_jiras.note: Later Published issue clarified resolve() discriminator targetProfile behavior on the same profiling page and supports keeping the FHIR-13399 conformance-based interpretation.
